activePlan.objective: Fix an unintended consequence of the release->main promotion automation: PR #9 (the permanent monitoring hook) was auto-merged and auto-closed by GitHub, and would keep recurring on every future promotion unless the monitoring hook's design changes.
steps: Diagnose the auto-merge: merging PR #10 (release -> main, 63a42ec) made development's history - including PR #9's exact head commit, since PR #9's head was the development branch ref directly - reachable from main, so GitHub auto-closed and auto-merged PR #9 with nobody touching its merge button.
Recognize this is structural: every future release promotion will do the same thing to whatever PR is currently serving as the monitoring hook, if that PR's head is development itself.

Per the owner's explicit direction, redesign the mechanism: create a dedicated ci-monitor branch whose own commits are distinct new commits copying development's tree content - never development's actual commit objects.
Add .github/workflows/sync-ci-monitor.yml (push:development trigger) to keep ci-monitor current this way, never by merging/rebasing/fast-forwarding development's real commits onto it.
Open PR #11 (ci-monitor -> main) as PR #9's replacement and subscribe to its activity.

Update AGENTS.md throughout: the absolute never-merge rule now names PR #11 and documents the incident and the fix, ci-monitor is added as an explicit branch-creation exception, and the 'Automatic CI monitoring' / 'CI on development' sections now reference PR #11 and sync-ci-monitor.yml.
Add matching test/workflow.test.js coverage for sync-ci-monitor.yml and the updated LOCKED_PR_NUMBERS/AGENTS.md text.
Run the full local suite plus every fast/offline audit before pushing.

completed: Created the ci-monitor branch (one commit, parent = main's tip, tree = development's tip at the time) and pushed it.
Opened PR #11 (ci-monitor -> main), draft, explaining both the PR #9 incident and why ci-monitor's design prevents recurrence. Subscribed to its activity.

Added .github/workflows/sync-ci-monitor.yml: on push to development, replaces ci-monitor's tree with development's current content and commits it as a new commit on top of ci-monitor's own separate history - never fetching or fast-forwarding development's real commits.
block-pr-7.yml's LOCKED_PR_NUMBERS is now '7 9 11'; its header comment records all three PRs' history (PR #7 manually merged, PR #9 auto-merged as a side effect, PR #11 current).

AGENTS.md's absolute branch-policy rule now names PR #11, documents the PR #9 auto-merge incident and root cause, explains ci-monitor's distinct-commit design and why it prevents recurrence, and lists ci-monitor as an explicit branch-creation exception. The 'CI on development' and 'Automatic CI monitoring' sections, and the main-promotion bullet's PR #9 cross-reference, were all updated to match.

Added two new test/workflow.test.js tests: one updated for LOCKED_PR_NUMBERS='7 9 11' plus PR #11 documentation, one new test asserting sync-ci-monitor.yml's trigger/permissions/commands and the corresponding AGENTS.md text.
verification: lint:workflows, docs:check, validate, audit:clutter, audit:privacy, and audit:security all pass.
remaining: Push this commit to development, confirm Self-Test/CodeQL/AI handoff policy green, then confirm sync-ci-monitor.yml actually fires on that push and commits a fresh snapshot onto ci-monitor - this is the mechanism's first real exercise (ci-monitor's current content was seeded manually, not yet by the automated workflow).
The owner should confirm 'block' is added as a required status check on main (Settings -> Branches -> Branch protection rules) if not already done - no tool available here can do that remotely.

Still blocked on owner-supplied resources, not a code gap: the hosted multi-repository integration workflow and connect-workflow.yml's activate phase both need a real target repository/token to actually be exercised.
Codex's own remaining items still stand: no promotion or branch-protection change is authorized without the owner's explicit instruction beyond what's already been done.
